steps.text: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Saute onion until tender and translucent. Stir in the curry powder. Add the chopped carrots, and stir until the carrots are coated. Pour in the vegetable broth, and simmer until the carrots are soft, about 20 minutes.
Transfer the carrots and broth to a blender, and puree until smooth. Pour back into the pot, and thin with water to your preferred consistency.

raw_recipe.headline: Curried Carrot Soup
raw_recipe.description: Carrots cooked in vegetable broth are pureed with curry powder and sauteed onions in this gorgeous vegetarian soup. Garnish with golden raisins or a dollop of sour cream.
raw_recipe.name: Curried Carrot Soup

review.reviewBody: Really tasty, a definate keeper. I added garlic with the onions and along with the curry powder, cumin and garam masala.

Dee-LISH! Definitely add the garlic with the onion, but then when adding the cumin, add also 1/2 tsp of garam masala and 1/2 tsp of cumin (the trifecta of Indian spices!). It gives the recipe a wonderful lift and is simply delightful.

We loved this soup! I don't like curry powder enough to put a tablespoon into anything I cook, but I decided to use half and then put the shaker on the table for those who wanted more curry flavor. It turned out great! 

We are vegan and wanted to add a little extra protein so I made baked, tofu croutons, by cubing super firm tofu and soaking it in a marinade of tamari sauce and garlic then rolling each piece in corn starch before baking . I put it in the oven at 425 degrees, for about 20 minutes, turning once about half way. These made a wonderful addition to the soup. Sprinkle a little cilantro over the top and enjoy!

I gave it 5 stars, but I must say I completely changed the recipe. I used this as a starting point. I had 4 lbs of locally grown pesticide free carrots that I had to use up, but i only used about 2 1/2 of them. I sauteed the onions with garlic. Added 2 tbsp of curry powder 1/2 tsp of garam masala and 1/2 tsp of ginger. As the carrots were cooking in the vegetable broth, I roasted some corn cut off the cob and a red onion on the stove in some coconut oil. I also cooked 1 cup of jasmine rice. I reserved some of the carrot mixture and about 1/2 the corn mixture and 1/2 the rice before pureeing everything else with an immersion blender. Then added the remainder of veggies and rice to give it some texture and topped it with a dollop of plain yogurt and ate it with some fresh bread from my bread maker. YUM!! Even my 4 and 6 year olds gobbled it up.

Delicious! I roasted the carrots, onions, and (added) 8 cloves of garlic in the oven. (400 degrees for 45 minutes or so, til the mixture is soft.) The veggies were lightly coated with Evoo and garlic salt before roasting. In my blender I puréed the roasted veggies with the broth and added 1 teaspoon of dried thyme. It made enough for two hungry people. Next time I will make two batches and serve with a salad and toasted bread.

I'd just made chicken stock, so I used that in place of vegetable broth. Although I like curry, I wondered if it might be a little harsh as the only seasoning. So, I substituted Garam Masala. The stick blender worked fine for pureeing the soup. I did add a little kosher salt when I sauteed the onions. (My stock was salt-free. If I'd used canned, I wouldn't have added salt.)

Great flavor. I used chicken broth to make it a little richer. I ended up using about 5 cups total to get the right consistency. At the end I added half a block of crumbled firm tofu to add protein. Next time, I'll probably only puree half of it so it will be chunkier.

Super tasty, super easy, super healthy! I made this and added just a pinch of salt along with a "block" of tofu for protein. After mixing it up with my immersion blender, the tofu was MIA and everyone who has tried it is shocked they've been "tricked" into trying tofu. I will be using it as a base for other creative concoctions (possible candidates for inclusion: apple, sweet potato, spinach, chopped walnuts, homemade plain yogurt, mint...so many possibilities!).

Ok, lots of changes to make it delicious because it is way too plain on its own (which is why I gave it 2 stars). I used chicken broth instead of water. Added 2 tsp of minced garlic, 1 tsp of minced ginger, 1/2 tsp tumeric, 1/2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp carriander, and just to add something extra I added potatoes to the cooking carrots. And of course salt and pepper to taste. I dont suggest adding garam masala to the soup, the cinnamon and cloves tend to make it less savory.

I cut the recipe in half because I didn't know who would eat it besides me. So this worked out to be 3 c. of sliced carrots, 1 14.5 oz can of chicken broth, 1 tsp of curry powder. I also added some garlic and ground pepper when sauteing the onions and 1 T. fresh parsley during the simmering. When I blended it up it was the PERFECT consistency for me. Tossed in a few shakes of salt too and it was delicious. Thank you for a great recipe for my extra garden carrots.

I roasted the diced carrots at 420 for 40 minutes (brushed with a little olive oil), added garlic, and used 1 tsp Indian/Madras curry ("dryer," less sweet, more cumin), and 2 tsp sweet curry (more cinnamon, nutmeg, clove and cardamom). Added 1 tsp fresh grated ginger. used half vegetable half chicken stock, and a little cream right before serving. Wow!
Added an extra half tbsp of curry, garlic and 1 small potato. Delicious and so easy.
An awesome soup! Made it with Penny’s “The Now Curry” and it was fantastic!

Really good! Half an onion because that’s what I had, almost double the curry powder because I like it , it was great. It’s too difficult for me to find a blender that is never used so I used an immersion blender, which was OK, except near the end the soup started popping out of the pot. It was a little dangerous! I was surprised at how sweet it was. Topped with a little fresh parsley on individual servings. Will make again.
it was really easy and worth the effort.

Excellent. I added turmeric, pepper, and cumin. I added a bit of 1/2 and 1/2, but it wasn't necessary. This is good hot and cold! A big hit with company. I made sourdough croutons for it. I think it would be good with a few salted pistachio nuts on top.

The overall recipe was good, although I think I prefer butternut squash to the carrots. I felt this wasn't the best use of my homegrown carrots. I did add garlic, harissa paste, butter (never use vegetables oils!), and left out the additional water. We ate the soup with a dollop of sour cream and a slice of homemade bread. Wonderful lunch for a rainy day.

Very tasty despite the fact that there was no salt or pepper. Don't need to salt anyway - high blood pressure. I added two large cloves of garlic and 1/2 teaspoon of cumin. Will definitely make this one again.

This was definitely underspiced and "thin". I added two tablespoons of butter and half a cup of condensed milk; half a tsp of onion salt and pepper to taste. I should have added garlic, too. I don't know what causes the bitter aftertaste. I cooked up a nice kielbasa and served that on the side, and the combination was excellent.
I increased the amount of curry and it was delicious.
